purpose: NEO KB MODEL VALIDATION Sections 5-8: trace the PRE-stage probability pipeline, its historical backtest evidence, baseline comparison, and red-team findings.

section_5_model_trace.critical_finding: Only win_probability is implemented anywhere in this codebase. cut_probability/top20_probability/top10_probability/top5_probability are always None in every *_PRE_PUBLIC_MASTER.json record for every tournament (confirmed empirically: 0/120 non-null for all four fields in both 2026090003 and OK_OPEN_2026 variants). There is no CUT/TOP20/TOP10/TOP5 model to audit -- these fields are structurally defined in the schema but never computed by any script.
section_5_model_trace.win_probability_producer: scripts/72_collect_ok_open_public_master.py -> src/klpga/models/inference.py::run_inference() -> src/klpga/models/candidates.py (model 'M4') -> written to *_PRE_WIN_FORECAST.json, merged into *_PRE_PUBLIC_MASTER.json by scripts/83_build_ok_open_pre_public_master.py.
section_5_model_trace.exact_method: Conditional-logit / softmax over the field, NOT Monte Carlo: score_i = z1_i + beta*z2_i; P(i) = softmax(-score_i / tau) across all entrants. tau and beta are the model's only 2 free parameters, fit by deterministic grid-refine MLE against historical winners.
section_5_model_trace.inputs: Exactly 2 features: prior_avg_round_score_to_par, prior_recent_form_10 (career scoring strength + recent 10-tournament form). NO Strokes Gained input, no K-Ranking input, no field-strength term, no course/context term -- confirmed explicitly disclosed in inference.py's own docstring: 'this v1 model contains no SG/GIR/driving/putting/course-par proxy of any kind'.
section_5_model_trace.volatility_treatment: Feature values are shrunk toward the training-fold population mean (weight = n/(n+k)) and standardized to a z-score using population std -- there is no per-player variance/spread term feeding the probability output directly.
section_5_model_trace.field_strength_treatment: Not modeled explicitly -- softmax is field-relative only through shared tau/beta and each player's own z-scores.
section_5_model_trace.course_context_treatment: None -- confirmed no course/context input exists anywhere in the 2-feature model.
section_5_model_trace.monte_carlo_iteration_count: N/A for this model (it is not a simulation). DEFAULT_N_SIMULATIONS=5000 exists in src/klpga/neo_win/round_update.py and r1_live_probability.py, but those belong to the SEPARATE, already-BLOCKED in-round R1-LIVE engine, not the PRE-stage win_probability producer.
section_5_model_trace.cut_rule: No cut rule exists for PRE win_probability (there is no cut_probability output at all). A cut fraction concept (DEFAULT_CUT_FRACTION=0.65, a disclosed neutral default, never a fitted value) exists only in the separate R1-LIVE engine.
section_5_model_trace.missing_data_fallback: A None feature value or n==0 sample shrinks fully to the training-fold population mean (z=0.0) -- 'not dropped, not fabricated', per candidates.py's apply_shrinkage_and_standardize(). Per-player diagnostic counts (zero_history_count, unmatched_count) are computed internally but NOT written into the public *_PRE_WIN_FORECAST.json artifact -- only player_id/win_probability/a thin provenance block are persisted, so a reader of the public artifact cannot tell which players were shrunk to the population default.
section_5_model_trace.probability_normalization: Enforced and verified: inference.py's _validate_invariants() hard-fails unless every probability is finite/non-negative and the field sums to 1.0 +/- 1e-6; math_utils.clip_and_renormalize() re-normalizes after an epsilon floor. Confirmed empirically: 2026090003_PRE_WIN_FORECAST.json's normalization.sum == 1.0 across 120 entrants.
section_5_model_trace.cross_field_monotonicity: STRUCTURALLY MOOT, not verified -- since cut/top20/top10/top5_probability are always None, no code anywhere checks or could check WIN <= TOP5 <= TOP10 <= TOP20 <= CUT. The contract required by this task's Section 6 (0 <= WIN <= TOP5 <= TOP10 <= TOP20 <= CUT <= 1) cannot be evaluated because 4 of its 5 terms do not exist.
section_5_model_trace.publication_gate_defect_confirmed: scripts/83_build_ok_open_pre_public_master.py and scripts/84_build_ok_open_pre_website_candidate.py both gate publication of win_probability (and the never-populated other four fields) on LIVE_PROBABILITY_MODEL_STATUS, imported from src/klpga/neo_win/r1_live_probability.py -- the status flag documented and defect-recorded for the SEPARATE R1-LIVE in-round Monte Carlo engine, not for M4. Script 83's own comment even flags the intent ('a separate, independently Red-Team-reviewed model change') while the code checks the wrong model's flag. This is a genuine governance/wiring gap: M4's own publication safety has never been evaluated by the gate that actually controls its visibility -- it is currently withheld for the right practical reason (BLOCKED) but for a documentation-mismatched reason.
section_5_model_trace.provenance_recorded: PRE_WIN_FORECAST.json carries schema_version, model_version='M4', model_features, future_data_excluded=true, per-record provenance {source_artifact, cutoff, database_sha256}. No weights/config file beyond code-level constants in candidates.py.

section_6_historical_backtest.scope_clarification: Two DISTINCT historical evaluation efforts exist in this project's history. Neither is a 'backtest of the KB-era PRE pipeline against KG/OK Open/KB outcomes' (that backtest is IMPOSSIBLE today -- see KB PRE FORECAST STATUS below) -- they are earlier, separate, already-completed leakage-safe walk-forward evaluations against a much larger historical corpus.

m4_win_probability_backtest.reference: docs/SITE_STRUCTURE_TODO.md section 10.1 ('M4 frozen as the v1 production model'), built on src/klpga/backtest/walk_forward.py's leakage-safe, point-in-time architecture (klpga.backtest.temporal.is_strictly_before enforced at every step).
m4_win_probability_backtest.sample: 95/92/90 eligible historical tournaments at eligibility thresholds 5/8/10 respectively, drawn from a real ~100-tournament production DB corpus.
m4_win_probability_backtest.result: M4 (prior_avg_round_score_to_par + prior_recent_form_10) had the best mean log loss at every threshold swept: 3.9856 (N=95), 3.9721 (N=92), 3.9870 (N=90). Paired Wilcoxon vs baseline M1 (career scoring strength only): mean_diff -0.1181/-0.1209/-0.1232 (M4 improves on M1), p-value 0.0444/0.0443/0.0442 at each threshold -- statistically significant at the conventional 0.05 level, but only marginally (all three p-values are within 0.006 of the threshold).
m4_win_probability_backtest.disclosed_unfixed_limitation: 'Coarse calibration diagnostics suggest over-confidence in some higher probability bins, especially approximately 10-20%. This is disclosed here as a known, accepted property of the v1 model -- not something this stage's inference layer attempts to correct via any post-hoc adjustment.' (SITE_STRUCTURE_TODO.md, section 10.1, verbatim). This limitation has never been remediated in any later phase of this project.

neo_ranking_v1_backtest.reference: docs/NEO_RANKING_V1_REDTEAM_BACKTEST.md -- a full leakage-safe historical backtest already exists for the SEPARATE NEO Ranking V1 composite formula (not M4, not the SG bands).
neo_ranking_v1_backtest.verdict_on_record: REJECT -- verbatim: 'V1은 validation-only heuristic이며 historical K-Ranking baseline 부재, 약한 순위/결과 상관, target-field archival limitation 때문에 PUBLIC/BETA 승격 근거가 없다.'
neo_ranking_v1_backtest.sample: 82 tournaments, 7830 player-event observations, 211 players; every feature date strictly precedes its target's start date (0 future-leakage violations).
neo_ranking_v1_backtest.performance: Mean Spearman (NEO rank vs finish) 0.4813; mean Spearman (NEO score vs subsequent SG Total) 0.4202; Top10 precision/recall 0.3366/0.3366; Top20 precision/recall 0.4902/0.4902; made-cut AUC 0.7120. Historical K-Ranking baseline comparison: NOT EVALUABLE (point-in-time K-Ranking snapshots do not exist; using today's snapshot as a historical baseline would itself leak future information).
neo_ranking_v1_backtest.hard_validation: future leakage: 0; duplicate event-player: 0; invalid player mapping: 0; insufficient-sample forcibly ranked: 0; reproducibility: deterministic, confirmed True/True.
documented_defects: heuristic weights double-count correlated recent5/recent10/long-term SG windows
cohort z-scores are event-relative and not calibrated across events
sample_reliability rewards high sample count rather than shrinking uncertainty
volatility penalized symmetrically, may suppress genuinely improving players
historical field reconstruction from retained SG rows misses unresolved/non-SG players
no point-in-time K-Ranking snapshot exists, blocking the K-vs-NEO incremental-value test
neo_ranking_v1_backtest.current_config_state_matches_verdict: content/website_v2/NEO_RANKING_VALIDATION_MODEL_V1.json's publication_class='VALIDATION_MODEL_NOT_PRODUCTION' and weight_status='HEURISTIC_FOR_EVALUATION_NOT_FITTED_OR_APPROVED' -- consistent with, and already correctly reflecting, the REJECT verdict above. No change needed; this task's own instruction not to retune the weights is honored -- the weights were never approved and remain unapproved.

section_6_historical_backtest.kb_specific_backtest: NOT PERFORMED and NOT POSSIBLE with current data -- see KB PRE FORECAST STATUS below. Zero of the four tournaments tracked in this system's TOURNAMENT_SITE_REGISTRY.json (KG Ladies Open, OK Open, KB, 하나금융그룹) has both a genuine non-reconstructed frozen PRE prediction AND a genuine confirmed FINAL result today, so a leakage-safe PRE-vs-actual test on THIS project's own tournament-by-tournament PRE/HOME pipeline (as opposed to the much larger historical corpus the M4/NEO-Ranking backtests above already used) cannot be run.

section_7_baselines.m4_vs_baseline: M4 was compared against M1 (career scoring strength only) in the walk-forward backtest above and won on mean log loss at all three swept thresholds, p~0.044 (marginal). No comparison against a pure field-rate/base-rate baseline (e.g. uniform 1/field_size for every player) or an SG-only baseline is on record for M4 -- M4 does not use SG at all, so an SG-only baseline comparison was never run for it.
section_7_baselines.neo_ranking_vs_baseline: The REDTEAM_BACKTEST explicitly could not compare NEO Ranking V1 against a historical K-Ranking baseline (point-in-time K-Ranking snapshots do not exist) -- this is an acknowledged, unresolved coverage gap, reported honestly rather than invented.
section_7_baselines.honest_conclusion: M4 demonstrates a modest, statistically marginal improvement over one simple baseline (M1) on one metric (log loss) -- it has not been shown to beat a field-rate/base-rate baseline or an SG-based baseline, and NEO Ranking V1 has never been compared to the one baseline (historical K-Ranking) that would matter most, purely for lack of available historical snapshot data.

section_8_red_team.future_leakage: 0 violations confirmed in both the M4 walk-forward evaluation and the NEO Ranking V1 backtest (both enforce klpga.backtest.temporal.is_strictly_before at every step).
section_8_red_team.survivorship_bias: Confirmed present in the SG warehouse: the identity-resolution defect (NEO_SG_FORENSIC_AUDIT_V1.json) systematically drops genuine multi-round cumulative SG records for players who did not appear on a tournament's FINAL round leaderboard (i.e., players who were cut or withdrew) in favor of a noisier single-round figure -- a real, confirmed survivorship-adjacent artifact, not a false-positive concern.
section_8_red_team.unequal_round_exposure: Documented in full in NEO_SG_FORENSIC_AUDIT_V1.json -- confirmed real, moderate severity, Spearman 0.918 vs a round-weighted challenger, Top10 stable, Top20 20% churn.
section_8_red_team.missed_cut_bias: The SG warehouse has no cut/WD/status field at all (confirmed by direct schema inspection) -- missed-cut players cannot be distinguished from withdrawals or from players who simply had an unresolved identity lookup. This is a genuine, unaddressed gap.
section_8_red_team.withdrawal_handling: No explicit WD handling exists in the SG warehouse pipeline; WD players are indistinguishable from cut players or identity-resolution failures (see above).
section_8_red_team.field_strength_distortion: M4 has no field-strength term (confirmed in section 5) -- a genuinely weak or strong week's field is not adjusted for.
section_8_red_team.small_sample_players: 8/120 TOP120 players have fewer than 5 total retained SG observations (NEO_SG_FORENSIC_AUDIT_V1.json) -- these are the players most exposed to any of the above artifacts.
section_8_red_team.missing_sg: home_ranking.build_features() returns eligibility='INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE' for players with fewer than 10 total observations -- correctly disclosed, never imputed.
section_8_red_team.amateur_invited_players: Not specifically audited in this pass -- no amateur/invited-status field was found in the entry_snapshot/current_player_master schemas examined; flagged as an open item, not resolved.
section_8_red_team.k_ranking_temporal_mismatch: Confirmed structural: the K-Ranking snapshot used for a tournament (e.g. 2026-W36 for KB) is the MOST RECENTLY AVAILABLE official ranking at build time, not necessarily the ranking in effect at the tournament's own start -- no point-in-time K-Ranking archive exists (same gap the NEO Ranking V1 backtest already flagged).
section_8_red_team.duplicate_player_event_records: NEO Ranking V1's backtest hard-validation confirmed 0 duplicate event-player records in its own dataset; the SG warehouse's dedup-by-max-rounds logic (home_ranking.build_features) is specifically designed to collapse duplicates but, per this audit, sometimes collapses to the WRONG (lower-information) row due to the identity-resolution defect.
section_8_red_team.probability_monotonicity: Cannot be evaluated -- see section 5 (4 of 5 required fields do not exist).
section_8_red_team.overconfidence: Explicitly disclosed and NOT fixed for M4 (SITE_STRUCTURE_TODO.md section 10.1: overconfidence in the ~10-20% probability bin).
section_8_red_team.winner_probability_concentration: Not independently re-tested in this pass; the existing M4 backtest's log-loss-based evaluation is sensitive to this but no dedicated concentration/calibration-curve artifact beyond the disclosed bin-level note was found.
section_8_red_team.tournament_specific_hardcoding: None found in the models/inference layer itself (M4's features and fitting are generic); the PUBLICATION GATE wiring defect (checking r1_live_probability's status instead of a model-specific one) is a governance bug, not tournament-specific hardcoding.
